The '''Perlemian Trade Route''', also known as the '''Axis''',<ref name="TEGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref><ref name="PH">{{FFG|story=Perlemian Haul (adventure)|book=Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|text=''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook}}</ref> was a vital trade [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroute]] that ran through the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. Along with the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]], it was one of the two routes that made up the border of [[The Slice/Legends|The Slice]]. It was founded c. [[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]], linking the young [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] with [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]]. The route took its name from the [[Perlemia system/Legends|Perlemia system]], located in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]],<ref name="EAOC" /> which in its early history produced the thousands of [[Scout ship/Legends|scout vessels]] that charted the route.<ref name="TEGtW" />

==Astrography==
It began at [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and passed the worlds of [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]], [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]], [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]], [[Carida/Legends|Carida]], [[Nak Shimor]], [[Taanab/Legends|Taanab]], [[Kulthis]], [[Sorjus]], [[Vaynai/Legends|Vaynai]], [[Columex/Legends|Columex]], and [[Estaria/Legends|Estaria]]. Beyond Estaria and the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]] the route became known as the [[Far Perlemian]], and passed through [[Makem Te/Legends|Makem Te]], [[Ter Abbes]], and terminated just past [[Quermia/Legends|Quermia]].<ref name="Xim Week" /> The Perlemian also passed the [[Roche asteroid field]], [[The Wheel/Legends|The Wheel]], and the [[Cron Drift/Legends|Cron Drift]].

==History==
The Route first connected Coruscant to Ossus, and Coruscanti reunited with the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], the ascetic warriors who left the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core]] centuries ago and remained but a myth until then. The Route contributed to the growth of the Republic since civilizations and colonies sued for protection from the Tionese and [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]. With the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]], it formed [[The Slice/Legends|The Slice]] region of the Galaxy which was explored and populated easier and faster than other parts. Further expansion of the Route led it up to the [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].

The forces of the Republic and of the [[Tion Hegemony/Legends|Tion Hegemony]] used the route extensively during the [[Tionese War]], where fleets from both powers raced back and forth along the Perlemian, dropping [[pressure bomb]]s on each other's capitals.

[[Cardan-class space station|''Cardan''-class space stations]] were present at the crossroads between the Perlemian Trade Route and the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]].

==Behind the scenes==
There seem to be two disparate accounts of the blazing of this hyperspace route. The first, and most referenced, points to a very early founding of the Route. ''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]'' notes "The first galactic scouts struck out from the Core Worlds along two stable hyperspace paths - the Perlemian Trade Route and the Corellian Run," and ''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]'' notes "A millennium after the fall of Xim the Despot, Human traders claiming to hail from the center of the galaxy visited the [[Tion Hegemony/Legends|Tion]] . . . Tion [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] fleets followed the new arrivals back down their so-called Perlemian Trade Route; there, they found rich planets bound in a loose, democratic union - and ill prepared for war." ''The New Essential Chronology'' indicates the Route was mapped between 25,000 BBY and 24,000 BBY. ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' further points out the Perlemian was formed at the time of the formation of the Republic and its [[Expansionist Period/Legends|Expansionist Period]].

However, ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' indicates a different history, suggesting that it was founded not long after the end of the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], resulting in the decline of worlds like Taris. This information cannot be reconciled with ''The Essential Atlas'' and ''The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons{{'}}'' accounts of the foundation of the Perlemian, so this article assumes that the former account is correct.
